Summary: The change closes Stack 8 and bumps the module to 0.2.8. It adds two gate checks: `version` (D-10 agreement across the manifest, the root module, the public .NOTES blocks, the CHANGELOG and, with -Base, the tags) and `package` (the .nupkg must hold exactly the files in FileList). It also adds a FileList check to Publish-ToGallery.ps1, makes its -ApiKey a SecureString that is extracted inline, tightens the `review` check so it refuses a record left by an earlier pull request, and adds four seeded cases, with documentation to match. I read REVIEW.md, AGENTS.md, the commit messages and the full diff in that order: intent, then tests, then implementation. I also read Build-Module.ps1, Publish-ToGallery.ps1, the relevant parts of Invoke-Gate.ps1 and the CI workflow (full fetch, so tags are present). The S-01/S-03 handling of the API key is correct, and the review-stale fix behaves as described. The findings are gaps in the new [SEC] file-list checks, a tag rule narrower than what it claims to protect, and a TODO item ticked before it can be done.

Findings.Title: The FileList check lists the version folder without -Force, so a hidden file passes the check but is still packaged and published.
Findings.Detail: `Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $stagingDir -File -Recurse` leaves out items with the Hidden or System attribute unless -Force is given. The comment next to the check, and the audit record, say that Publish-PSResource packages every file in the version folder, so a hidden file in that folder is not in `$onDisk`, does not show up in `$extra`, and goes to PSGallery, where a version can never be removed. This is the last check before publishing, and it runs on a local folder that the gate's `package` check never saw. Fix: add `-Force` to the Get-ChildItem call. Better still, compare against the entries of the package Publish-PSResource actually builds, as Build-Module.ps1 does.
Findings.Response: Fixed: 1858ee6. Get-ChildItem now lists the version folder with -Force, so a hidden or system file is compared with FileList before publishing.

Findings.Title: The package comparison drops some entries before it compares, so a stray file whose path matches those filters is never seen.
Findings.Detail: `$packaged` is built from `$entries`, which already leaves out any entry under `_rels/` or `package/`, any entry whose name starts with `[`, and any entry ending in `.nuspec` at any depth. That filter was written to tidy the contents listing. It now also feeds the new [SEC] check, so a file in the version folder such as `package/x`, `notes.nuspec` or `[draft].txt` would be packaged and still pass the 'exactly the FileList files' check. Fix: exclude only the exact NuGet metadata entries (the root `[Content_Types].xml`, `_rels/.rels`, `package/services/metadata/...` and the root `<id>.nuspec`), and compare everything else.
Findings.Response: Fixed: 1858ee6. The comparison now leaves out only the exact entries NuGet adds ([Content_Types].xml, _rels/.rels, the root TACE.Oracle.Admin.nuspec and the core-properties .psmdcp); every other entry is compared with FileList.

Findings.Title: The tag rule treats a released version as changed only when files under Source/ change, but the package also depends on README.md, LICENSE and Build-Module.ps1.
Findings.Detail: Decision 36 and SECURITY section 13 say the tag rule keeps a released number from labelling different code or contents. The check looks only at `Source/*` in `$baseCommit...HEAD`. Build-Module.ps1 merges Source into the shipped .psm1 and copies README.md and LICENSE (`$rootFiles`) into the package. A pull request that edits the build script's merge logic or the README, without bumping the version, produces a different package under an already-tagged version and passes `version`. Fix: count changes to `README.md`, `LICENSE` and `Scripts/Build-Module.ps1` as well, or narrow the wording in the documents to 'Source\'.
Findings.Response: Fixed: 1858ee6. The tag rule now counts README.md, LICENSE and Scripts/Build-Module.ps1 as well as Source/, the files the package is made from; decision 36, SECURITY section 13, PREREQUISITES, VERSIONING and the CHANGELOG say so.

Findings.Title: TODO marks tag v0.2.8 as done, but the documents say the tag is made by hand after the merge, so it cannot exist at this commit.
Findings.Detail: SECURITY.md (section 13 and step 2 of the release procedure), PREREQUISITES and decision 36 all say the tag goes on the merge commit after the pull request merges, and the gate's own tag-rule comment says a release's pull request passes with its version not yet tagged. The TODO line '[x] `CHANGELOG.md` 0.2.8 and tag `v0.2.8`' therefore records work that has not been done, and STAGES already marks Stack 8 'Complete (v0.2.8)'. Fix: leave the tag as an open item until it is made, or reword the line so it says the tag follows the merge.
Findings.Response: Rejected: under the close-once pattern the closing tasks are ticked in the stack pull request, and the tag is made on the merge commit immediately after it merges, as for v0.2.7. Leaving the line open would need a follow-up pull request only to tick it.
